h1: Chumphon Gardens Hotel — A City Hotel Whose Breakfast Brings Guests Back
intro: If you want a place in central Chumphon with roomy rooms, soft beds, and a generous breakfast, Chumphon Gardens Hotel is a name that comes up often — a city hotel close to the municipal fresh market and less than a kilometre from Chumphon Railway Station. What guests agree on most is the varied, tasty breakfast buffet, followed by rooms that are bigger than expected and plenty of parking space. Around 70 rooms, from approx. ฿700/night · 8.6 from real guest reviews.

body.html: Chumphon Gardens Hotel is a city hotel that has been open since around 2007, and it remains a popular pick for travellers stopping in Chumphon. It has roughly 70 rooms — mostly Superior rooms plus a couple of suites. The Superior rooms run about 25 square metres, which is generous for this price bracket. The hotel doesn't go for a modern look, but it's well set up for a rest, with AC, TV, a fridge, and bathrooms that guests describe as clean.

The thing reviews mention most is the breakfast buffet. Many say the spread is varied and tastes better than you'd expect from a budget hotel — Thai dishes, rice porridge, eggs and sweets. Some packages include it; on others it costs around ฿150 per person, which people who tried it say is worth it. This is the reason a fair few reviewers happily return whenever they pass through Chumphon.
"Roomy room, soft comfortable bed, loads of parking — but the best part was breakfast. The buffet had plenty of choice and was tasty. At this price, great value."

Location is another plus. The hotel sits in central Chumphon, close to the municipal fresh market with food easy to find on foot, and less than a kilometre from Chumphon Railway Station — walkable with a bag, or a short ride. There are convenience stores and restaurants nearby, so dinner is easy in the evening. The parking is a standout that self-drivers mention often, since there's plenty of space and no scramble for a spot.

What you'll need to accept is the age of the building and the décor. Open for more than fifteen years, parts of the rooms and the carpets look their age, and some reviews note the mattresses in certain rooms are starting to sag. There's no pool and no gym, so it isn't the place for a resort feel. Service draws mixed views — most say staff are helpful, but a few felt responses were slow at times.

For onward travel, this suits people using Chumphon as a base before a ferry to Koh Tao or Koh Phangan, or continuing by train. The piers around Pak Nam Chumphon are roughly a 20–25 minute drive away, and the hotel can help arrange tickets and transport. Chumphon's nicer beaches, Sai Ri and Thung Wua Laen, are further out and better suited to travellers with a car.

Honestly, Chumphon Gardens Hotel isn't new or fancy, but if the goal is roomy rooms, an easy price, comfortable parking, and a good breakfast in a central spot near the market and station, it does that job well for the money. It's an ideal one- to two-night base while you travel. If you want modern new rooms or facilities like a pool, you may prefer another option in the roundup.

honestSummary: Chumphon Gardens Hotel is the city hotel for travellers who want roomy rooms, an easy price, comfortable parking, and a good breakfast near the market and railway station — a tidy base while you travel or before a ferry to the islands. Just accept that the building is old, some mattresses sag, and there are no resort facilities.
honestChecks: If you want new rooms and a firm mattress — open for more than fifteen years, some rooms' mattresses are starting to sag → ask to see a room first or request one in better condition at check-in.
If you want a resort feel or a sea view — this is a city hotel with no pool and no beach → look at the Sai Ri or Thung Wua Laen beachfront options in the roundup instead.
If you want breakfast at the hotel — some packages don't include it, with a charge of about ฿150 per person → confirm at booking, as many guests say it's worth paying for.

faq.q: Where is Chumphon Gardens Hotel, and how close is the railway station?
faq.a: It's at 66/1 Tha Taphao Road, Tha Taphao, Mueang Chumphon, right in the city centre, close to the municipal fresh market (about a 7-minute walk) · it's less than 1 km from Chumphon Railway Station — walkable with a bag or a short ride away.

faq.q: How much does Chumphon Gardens Hotel cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿700/night for a Superior room of around 25 sqm · there are twin and double options, a version with breakfast included, and a Suite (about ฿1,200). Prices vary by season and package, so compare a few platforms before you book.

faq.q: What is the breakfast like at Chumphon Gardens Hotel?
faq.a: Breakfast is a buffet, and it's the most-praised part in reviews — varied and tastier than you'd expect from a budget hotel · some packages include it, on others it's about ฿150 per person, which many guests say is worth it.

faq.q: Who is Chumphon Gardens Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for travellers who want roomy rooms, an easy price, comfortable parking, and a good breakfast in a central spot · a tidy base before a ferry to Koh Tao or Koh Phangan, or for continuing by train · if you want a beachfront resort or modern new rooms, another option may suit you better.

faq.q: Does Chumphon Gardens Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: There is spacious free parking, a standout that self-drivers mention often · but there's no pool and no gym, as this is a straightforward city hotel — if you want a pool, look at the beachfront options in the roundup instead.

faq.q: How do I get from Chumphon Gardens Hotel to the Koh Tao ferry?
faq.a: The piers for Koh Tao and Koh Phangan are around Pak Nam Chumphon, roughly a 25-minute drive away · hotel staff can help arrange ferry tickets and transport to the pier · flag it at check-in so they can time it for the ferry you want.
